justification: Fresh judgement first, then round 1. On a phone and on a desktop, in both themes, this page is visibly better presented than Pro Git 3.2 and the Git Tower conflict chapter. Pro Git has eight figures but no exercises, no tables, no dark theme and nothing on index stages, diff3, --abort, delete/binary conflicts or strategies; Git Tower has one command block, one marker diagram and a Kaleidoscope screenshot, and no depth on stages, diff3, binary or delete conflicts. Here: a delivering first paragraph, short prose runs alternating with paired BASH/OUTPUT panels, a clear h2/h3 hierarchy with content-specific headings, four figures that each show structure prose cannot (ref move, three-snapshot merge with parent 1/2, stage 1/2/3 to stage 0, three-parent octopus commit), captions that say what to notice, theme-correct colours in dark (accent/bad/good boxes re-tinted; I found nothing wrong in dark or light), a 4-row table that fits at 390 px, one well-placed pitfall and one note callout, three exercises of different forms mid-article, and a 15-item source list in which every entry is cited inline. Collapsed on-this-page on mobile, sticky TOC on desktop, fade-out edge on scrollable code, and 'Exits with an error' badges on the two intentional failures are all good. Round-1 check: every design major is fixed. The strategies table is now a bullet list (no clipping); the --is-ancestor block is split so && and || are on screen (mobile part03); the sed lines in the conflict setup are split with backslashes; commit messages and the branch -d pipe are split; the octopus figure (Figure 4) exists; the index paragraph is split into a list plus separate paragraphs; the macOS sed note is now a callout before the first sed block. Round-1 minor on the author box boilerplate is still open (shell-level). What holds it at 8.5 rather than higher: three output panels still clip at 390 px (Git's own text, so partly unavoidable, and each is clipped on the non-operative half), the Resolve/stage/commit subsection is about four desktop screens and ends in three consecutive dense paragraphs about combined diffs, and the article talks about the phone in its own prose. None of this is shell breakage; nothing is a blocker or major.

issues.location: Output panels at 390 px: 'git merge rename-latte' (mobile-dark-part10: 'CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in men…', 'Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and…'); three-way merge output (part07: '2 files changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 dele…'); clean-but-wrong merge output (part18: '1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deleti…')
issues.problem: Git's own lines are wider than about 40 columns and are cut, so a phone reader has to scroll sideways to see the file name in the CONFLICT line and the 'insertions/deletions' summary. The conflict case is softened because the next paragraph quotes 'fix conflicts and then commit the result' and names menu.txt, and the panel fades at the edge to signal scroll, so this is a nit, not a defect. The diffstat summary lines carry no information the reader needs.
issues.fixLooksLike: Drop the noisy summary lines from the outputs (pipe through 'grep -v files\ changed' or 'sed $d', as the article already does for --stat elsewhere), and for the CONFLICT lines either pipe through 'fold -s -w 40' so the full text wraps inside the panel, or keep as is and leave the following paragraph quoting the clipped words. Re-run verify and check mobile part10 and part18.

issues.location: Section 'Conflicts with no lines to edit', paragraph after the 'git merge right' output ('The first line is cut short on a phone: it reads ...') and the [...] wildcards in that output
issues.problem: The output panel hides the informative half of every CONFLICT line behind [...] (on desktop too, where there is room), and the prose then mentions that the line is 'cut short on a phone'. That is a workaround shown to the reader: the article comments on its own layout, and a desktop reader sees a panel that omits text for no visible reason. The 'delete/binary/add-add' explanation is the payoff of this section, and the exact Git messages are what a reader will search for when they hit them.
issues.fixLooksLike: Show the real messages wrapped to 40 columns (for example 'git merge right 2>&1 | fold -s -w 40' with the run harness wildcarding only the volatile parts), and delete the sentence about phones. If the text must stay abbreviated, say why in terms of Git ('Git also prints the file names; they are elided here') rather than in terms of the screen.

issues.location: Section 'Resolve, stage, commit' from the 'git show' output to the 'Exercise 2' block (desktop-light part10 to part11, mobile-dark part14 to part16)
issues.problem: This one h3 covers scripted resolution, the pitfall, git add/commit, the combined diff, two filters, what an empty combined diff proves, and --remerge-diff. On mobile the three paragraphs starting 'Two filters decide...', 'So read the combined diff...' and 'To see what the resolver did...' run about 26 wrapped lines with 8 to 10 inline code spans and no code, figure or list to break them. Desktop is fine; on a phone it is the only real wall of text on the page.
issues.fixLooksLike: Give the post-merge inspection its own h3 ('Reading the merge commit afterwards') so the TOC exposes it, and either turn the two filters into a two-item list or trim the 'Only files that differ from every parent are listed' explanation to the one sentence a reader needs. Keep --remerge-diff with its output.

issues.location: Headings 'The merge commit has two parents' and 'What Git leaves behind when it stops' (desktop-light part06 and part07)
issues.problem: Each h3 is followed directly by a code block with no lead-in sentence, unlike every other section which introduces its block. The h3 then reads as a caption for the block rather than the start of an explanation, and the block's purpose is only clear after the output.
issues.fixLooksLike: Add one sentence before each block saying what to look for ('The graph now has two lines joining at the top; then ask Git for each parent separately.').

issues.problem: The first paragraph packs three outcomes, a fourth case, a doc link and a long inline flag ('--allow-unrelated-histories') that wraps mid-token at 390 px ('--allow-' / 'unrelated-histories'). It is 15 lines on a phone. The content is good and the first sentence delivers; the length and the wrapped flag are what hurt.
issues.fixLooksLike: Move the parenthetical about unrelated histories to its own short sentence after the three outcomes, or into a note callout; keep the paragraph to the three outcomes.
